title: O Jesus, When I Think of Thee
description: O Jesus, When I Think of Thee in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 8 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Latin hymns of the early Church for Hymns of the Early Church (London, 1896), headed “Monday Evening”.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Common Metre (8.6.8.6), and this page sets them to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O Je-sus, when I think of Thee, True glad-ness fills my heart; But joy un-speak-a-ble ’twill be To see Thee as Thou art.

lines: O Jesus, when I think of Thee,
True gladness fills my heart;
But joy unspeakable ’twill be
To see Thee as Thou art.
O blessed name! No note more sweet,
No music so divine;
Its charms the dearest fancies greet
That with my memory twine.
To those who come with sin confessed,
Thy name their hope inspires;
And every needy soul is blessed,
And granted all desires.
To those who seek, ah! Thou art found
Far more than all desire—
A living fount whose streams abound,
A flame of heavenly fire.
What tongue can e’er the charm express?
What words its beauty show?
For Thy dear name’s sweet loveliness
No heart can ever know.
Who only taste the heavenly bread,
They hunger for the feast;
Who drink of Christ, the Fountainhead,
But find their thirst increase.
O Jesus, to my fainting heart
When wilt Thou come to speak?
O, when to me Thy bliss impart,
And more than I can seek?
O I will feed and hunger still,
O I will drink and pine
Till Thou my famished spirit fill
With that blest name of Thine.

source: John Brownlie, Hymns of the Early Church (1896)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Latin, public domain, as printed in Hymns of the Early Church; set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
